findings.evidence: “This skill is a Process … executed with Tool-level rigor” names rubric patterns rather than helping the agent make a decision. The following factory-command requirement and its failure rationale are useful project knowledge.
findings.fix: Keep the requirement to use the factory subcommands and the reason; record removal of only the rubric labels.

findings.evidence: “### Step 1 — Detect” and the remaining phases are nested under “## NEVER,” while Step 0 is under “## Your task.” The heading tree puts the main procedure inside the anti-pattern list.
findings.fix: Make Steps 0–4 peer headings, with each substep under its own phase, preserving the heading text and existing links.

findings.evidence: “Use when the user requests cross-AI review or execute setup” gives the main trigger but omits the distinction between setup and running with an existing roster. “Migrates an old review-spec.toml on first use” also does not tell the agent when a migration-only request should trigger the skill.
findings.fix: Use when the user wants to choose, test or reorder the CLIs and models that review plans or execute work in ai-kit, even if they don't call them lanes; when a review or execute run offers setup because no roster exists; or when the user asks to check availability, investigate stale provider references or check migration from review-spec.toml. Configures separate review and execute orders in the [lanes] table of .aikit/config.toml, with --local or --global to select the layer and explicit consent before replacing an existing roster. Use --check-only to report availability without persisting config, cache or trust changes. A migration-only request reports what is pending. Do not use to run a review or execution with existing lanes, hand-edit a single lane or tune [runner] settings.

findings.evidence: The body remains under 500 lines but is over 6,000 words, including the full “When the write target was local” trust procedure on every load, even for check-only and global setup. The existing references are otherwise well gated.
findings.fix: Keep the local command-bearing decision and explicit-consent requirement in Step 4. Move the trust-preview procedure, including its migration, inherited-command and role-specific caveats, into references/config-file.md and load that section only for a command-bearing local roster or an untrusted-local warning.

findings.evidence: “--global forces <user config> directly” and “--local also forces local directly” leave the destination ambiguous if both are supplied. The replacement gate does not resolve that scope conflict on a fresh target.
findings.fix: Treat --local and --global as mutually exclusive. If both are passed, stop before snapshot persistence or target selection and ask the owner to rerun with one.

findings.evidence: “If the proposal shows an alias group” can pass even if the known alias disappears. The supplied fixture names an alias, but does not establish that the proposal must receive and surface it.
findings.fix: Give the alias eval a deterministic installed-runtime and catalog fixture, then require the named alias to appear unranked, with its provenance label and without a heuristic confirmation question.

findings.evidence: “Plan the next GSD phase for the usage metrics dashboard feature” is an easy negative, unlike the stronger existing cases that distinguish running with configured lanes from configuring them.
findings.fix: Replace the unrelated negatives with near-misses such as asking why an already-configured lane was skipped during a review, or asking to change only the model-catalog source settings.

findings.evidence: “Do not run fetch-model-catalog” protects an unapproved legacy roster in Step 1.5, but a preferred runtime without a model list sends the wizard to references/cli-model-selection.md:31, which runs the same migrating fetch again. On a cold cache, the skip branch also leaves no catalog for the proposal or the explicit --catalog-path on the writer.
findings.fix: Carry the migration decision into every fetch and retry. If an unapproved roster is pending, use a roster-read-only discovery path; if none is available, skip catalog-dependent commands and either continue with owner-named lanes and the writer's optional catalog argument omitted, or stop without touching the pending roster.

findings.evidence: “Show its command text from the file” cannot work for an omitted command-bearing override that inherits its template from the user config. A flattened preview keyed only by lane key also cannot establish which role's arguments were shown.
findings.fix: Require a role-qualified preview of the effective merged argv for every command-bearing entry, including inherited commands and their substituted arguments. If any entry cannot be rendered, explain which entry is missing and leave the local roster untrusted.

findings.evidence: “Any runtime but claude and copilot” sends a Grok or custom lane through the --runtime effort-probe recipe even though the same workflow stores it with a command and no runtime. The probe implementation explicitly treats a command-only entry as unsupported for lane effort.
findings.fix: Offer the unknown-effort probe only for runner-backed pairs with an effort path. For Grok and other custom commands, state that the lane effort probe is unsupported and proceed to the separately consented command usability check.

findings.evidence: “config = cfg_resolve('$(pwd)', deps.env_fn(), migrate=False)” embeds the checkout path in a Python string literal, so an ordinary path containing an apostrophe breaks the preflight. The next branch permits a live probe when “none was printed” without distinguishing successful empty JSON from preflight failure.
findings.fix: Pass the project and helper paths as arguments rather than interpolating them into Python source. Require exit 0 and a parsed JSON array before a live probe; if preflight fails, report availability as unknown and continue only with the read-only provider report.
